policy.completion_rule: A domain may set domain_complete=true only when every required capability is exactly 'complete'. 'runtime_pass' is a narrow controlled observation and never closes a domain by itself.
policy.banner_rule: Every domain publishes status_banner verbatim in STATUS.md. The banner is '<title>: INCOMPLETE' while domain_complete is false and '<title>: COMPLETE' only when it is true.
policy.policy_text: A narrow fixture, golden, or single controlled run proves one fact and never closes a domain function. Full stateful completion requires the client/wire path, database persistence, reconnect projection, and the negative paths together. Every handoff must name the next missing behavior for each open domain.

capabilities.title: Backpack open and display
capabilities.notes: The client renders the persisted three-item Backpack as 3/40 with identities 1, 2 and 4 at slots 0, 1 and 3. This is one controlled observation of the projection, not a proof of every bag size, page, or filter.

capabilities.title: Move any known item to any free slot 0-39
capabilities.notes: GT-002 (attended, HEAD 55c7c59) delivered the first real-client acceptance: a drag of identity 1 from slot 0 to free slot 10 under the opt-in scenario produced the wire request, an explicit HYP_PF_010 commit response (82 bytes, 0.3 ms), the slot update in character_backpack_items plus the touched character_backpacks.updated_at, and a reconnect projection at slot 10. capabilities.title: Same-slot move is an exact no-op
capabilities.notes: Same-slot move is a silent no-op with no reply and no write, and stays one under replay. Runtime-proven at the wire/DB layer under the default free-slot profile by SAME-SLOT-NOOP-001 (three own-slot targets x three replays each, all silent, both persistence tables byte-identical before and after; heartbeat control confirms a live socket). It is accepted HYP-PF-010 behavior (the free-slot lane returns the same-slot None sentinel), not a new hypothesis; the swap milestone proved the same silence once under the swap profile. No client-observable claim: a no-op has no visible effect.

capabilities.title: Negative paths: unknown identity, out-of-range slot, malformed, replay, session and account isolation
capabilities.notes: Offline negative coverage exists for unknown identity, out-of-range slot, malformed, and replay. MOVE-ISOLATION-001 (chief round 67, 2026-08-18) adds the previously-missing isolation evidence: on a real server over TCP, two dev-account characters with identical INITIAL Backpacks each committed the byte-identical free-slot move under its own serial session, and each move mutated only its own character_id rows (the other character's rows and updated_at byte-identical across the foreign move), proving cross-session/cross-character isolation and within-session identity resolution. Two independent layers are proven: (Layer 1, wire) parse_item_operate_req decodes exactly operation/destination/item_identity with no owner field and rejects trailing bytes, so no request can name another character; (Layer 2, persistence) the _require_selected_session guard accepts only the open session that has itself selected that character within its own account, exercised against a seeded second account to reject foreign-account, unselected-sibling, and closed-session cases. Stays in_progress, not runtime_pass: full cross-account isolation at runtime needs two live authenticated accounts, which the development login path does not yet support (the standing authenticated_multi_account / persistence-accounts question). production_allowed stays false; the lane is opt-in only.

capabilities.title: Occupied destination with a different item: swap, displacement or reject
capabilities.notes: HYP-PF-017 (round 65): occupied-by-different-identity swap landed behind the dedicated swap profile of the item-move opt-in scenario, wire/DB headless-proven on a real server process over real TCP (two-item delta response byte-exact after the atomic commit; both persistence tables; canonical untouched). Outside that profile occupied destinations stay fail-closed exactly as pinned by HYP-PF-010 (probe pass E). Client-observable acceptance and the real client request shape for an occupied-destination drag are GT-015 (attended). Original-server policy remains unknown and unclaimed; production_allowed stays false.

capabilities.title: Compatible stack merge and stack limit behavior
capabilities.notes: One exact V111 merge to quantity 2 is runtime-proven and persisted (the real client accepted and rendered the original server's stack-merge delta live). ITEM-MERGE-001 (HYP-PF-018, chief round 71, 2026-08-18) generalizes that single captured behavior behind the dedicated merge profile of the item-move opt-in scenario: on a real server over real TCP, a strict-parse move onto a slot occupied by a same-template, identical-variant governed item merges the source stack into the surviving target in one atomic transaction against both named persistence tables, answered with the V111 merge delta structure byte-identically (the exact V111 direction reproduces the frozen V141 golden byte-for-byte; a generalized slot-7 instance committed with the same structure); different templates and the reversed direction fail closed, and the lane is unreachable without the opt-in profile. Client acceptance of the merge delta at non-slot-0 destinations rides GT-015 (attended). The stack ceiling, overflow split-on-merge behavior, and the original server's incompatible-template policy remain unproven and unclaimed; production_allowed stays false.

capabilities.title: Split a stack
capabilities.notes: SPLIT-OPERATE-001 (chief round 68, 2026-08-18) captures the request transport and its wire schema byte-exact from the client binary. A stack-split has no dedicated opcode: every item action rides ItemOperateVitalReq 0x4BED, discriminated by a single operation byte at obj+0x14 (wire tag 0x0B). The full operation space present in the image is {1,3,4,5,6}: 1 is the constructor default, and producers emit 3,4,5,6 as immediates. op4=move (value32=destination slot, qword=item identity) and op5=equip-from-bag (value32=slot bitfield) match the server's two recognized operations. op6 is the quantity-parameterized producer: its caller pops a positive-only numeric input dialog (0x5A1630) and encodes the entered count into the qword field (tag 0x32) that move/equip use for item identity, while value32 carries the item handle. This operation-dependent field meaning is the trap a naive split implementation would hit. The serializer 0x5E5AF0 and id assignment match the shared VitalData cohort (id 0x4BED is runtime-assigned, never a code immediate). Server gap: current/pf_login_game_server_v141.py handles operation 4 and 5 only; operations 3 and 6 have client producers but no server handler, so split is characterized, not implemented. Not claimed: op6 == split specifically (op6 is the quantity-op family covering split/drop-N/sell-N; op6 carries no destination slot, so distinguishing split needs the verb-code->UI action resolution for eax==0x16 or a live capture). Response lane = ItemOperateVitalRes 0x4C13 (shared with move-merge success); persistence lane = character_backpack_items rows + character_backpacks.updated_at under the pinned _require_selected_session guard. SPLIT-OPERATE-002 (chief round 69, 2026-08-18) enumerates the op6 family byte-exact and bounds the split candidate. The op6 factory 0x59F870 has exactly four call sites (0x57D1F4, 0x58294D, 0x5A3532, 0x5BA208), so op6 is definitively a shared quantity-op family, not a split opcode; every site passes (qty_low, qty_high, item_handle) and the factory serializes value32=item_handle and qword=64-bit quantity (ret 0xC) with no destination-slot argument at any site. The inventory action dispatcher is one function [0x5A2A70,0x5A40B0) that holds the op4=move producer call (verb eax==2 @0x5A3491) and exactly one op6 site (verb eax==0x16 @0x5A3532); the other three op6 sites are in three distinct functions outside it. So within the backpack move/equip dispatcher, verb 0x16 is the unique quantity-op path (opens numeric-input dialog resource 0x12, guards it strictly positive, then calls op6) and is the bounded split candidate. Still not claimed: verb 0x16 == split specifically -- op6-with-no-destination is equally consistent with backpack drop-N/destroy-N, so a positive split label still needs the dialog-resource 0x12 caption resolution or a live capture. SPLIT-OPERATE-003 (chief round 70, 2026-08-18; reports/PF_SPLIT_OPERATE003_VERB16_TWO_PANELS_STATIC_20260818.md, tools/pf_split_operate_verb_panels_static.py, tests/test_split_operate_verb_panels_static.py) walks that hop as far as static evidence allows and closes the static caption route. Two of the four op6 sites gate on cmp eax,0x16 (site C @0x5A3532 in the dispatcher fn 0x5A2A70, and site D @0x5BA208 in a distinct fn @0x5B9F70), both routing through the same numeric-input helper 0x5A1630 before op6 -- so verb 0x16 is not globally unique; the shared action code plus shared dialog is consistent with a generic quantity-split reused across panels but is still not a positive split label (op6 has no destination slot; equally consistent with a shared drop-N/destroy-N). The numeric dialog is the generic reusable control Common_NumInput.model (plaintext UIControlData XML with no inline caption); the caption text is resolved at runtime from the packed table B_TEXTDATA_TH.pc_ (magic $pcz) and packed UI Lua, so no readable client asset maps dialog id 0x12 to a split caption. Incidental correction: 0x42AB40 in the verb-0x16 body is a temp-object destructor (SEH prologue + two vtable stores + free 0x88D060), not a dialog opener; dialog id 0x12 is a stack local at 0x5A34D7. Net: the static caption route is now evidenced-closed, so the sole remaining hop to a positive split label is a live capture of the verb-0x16 numeric dialog plus the op6 frame it emits (queued as GT-015). Stays in_progress, not runtime_pass: no server handler and no runtime capture yet.

capabilities.title: Use, drop and sell paths
capabilities.notes: USE-DROP-SELL-001 (chief round 75, 2026-08-18) characterizes, byte-exact from the read-only client binary cross-checked against the read-only server source, how the client actually produces the use, drop and sell paths, and the headline is a pair of positive negatives: neither use nor sell rides ItemOperate at all. USE has its own request class UseItemVital (vtable 0xF30950, single registration 0xBEE600 into id-slot 0x1082030, one get-id stub 0x5BEA50, cohort-shaped like ItemOperateVitalReq) whose serializer 0x6C0180 emits exactly one field, a qword tag 0x32 at +0x18: use(item_identity) with no operation byte and no value32. SELL has an entire system of its own: StallModule_Client, StallStartVital, StallOpenVital and StallOperateVital for player stalls, the GSCN_BlackMarketPutOnSale/OffSale/Buy/Search family, UpdateConditionalStoreItemVital, and the ItemMall classes; StallOperateVital's serializer 0x76A630 is a priced wire (u8 tag 0x08 at +0x14, qword tag 0x32 at +0x18, u32 tag 0x14 at +0x20 = price, string at +0x24), a different shape from ItemOperate's three-field wire. None of the five functions that produce an ItemOperate (0x57CF50, 0x582730, 0x5A2A70, 0x5B9F70, 0x5B9CE0) references any string containing stall, market, store, sell, buy, shop, vendor, money or price, which retires the sell-N candidate SPLIT-OPERATE-002 had left open for the op6 family. Within ItemOperate the milestone pins op3: its single caller 0x5B9D0C sits in a 0x3E-byte function [0x5B9CE0,0x5B9D1E) that is never e8-called -- its only image-wide dword reference is push 0x5B9CE0 at 0x5BA16C, registering it as a dialog callback through 0x405D40 into dialog+0x12CC -- and it emits op3 only when [arg1+0x94]==1, reading the identity out of the global qword 0x1080F40/44 and clearing it; the latch is set by verb eax==2 of panel 0x5B9F70, which opens message-box template 0x69 first. So op3 is destructive-shaped: single target, identity-only, no quantity, no destination, no counterparty, behind a modal confirm. The three remaining op6 sites are separated: site A 0x57D1F4 in 0x57CF50 is a third verb-0x16 site that earlier rounds missed because it is written as a memory operand (cmp dword [esi+0x94],0x16) and it carries two item handles and follows op6 with two op5 equips; site B 0x58294D in 0x582730 is not verb-gated at all but gated on a context field [ctx+8] with a GetAsyncKeyState SHIFT/CTRL arm; site D 0x5BA208 is the verb-0x16 arm of panel 0x5B9F70. Server gap: v141 declares USE_ITEM_VITAL = 0x1F4F and lists it in NAMES but has no dispatch branch for it, ItemOperate accepts only operations 4 and 5 with no 3 and no 6, there is no stall or black-market id anywhere, the one implemented shop route is TradeCmdVital 0x23B5 which accepts a single command (cart-add/buy = 6) with no sell branch, and foundation runtime.py fails closed on every operation other than 4. Incidental evidenced correction: the mov dword [esp+0x180],0x12 at 0x5A34D7 that SPLIT-OPERATE-001/002 labelled a numeric-input dialog resource is in fact an MSVC EH trylevel store (the same slot takes 0xFFFFFFFF at 0x5A3502 and 0x0A at 0x5A335A/0x5A30C0, anchored by the EHRec lea/mov fs:[0]); this does not disturb any structure those rounds proved and it strengthens SPLIT-OPERATE-003's negative closure, because there was never a dialog id to resolve a caption for. Not claimed: that op3 is specifically drop, discard or destroy (the message-box 0x69 caption lives in the packed text table, so op3 remains compatible with destroy, discard, unequip-with-confirm or consume-with-confirm), that any op6 verb is split or drop-N, and that the client has no drop request at all. Status is in_progress, not runtime_pass: no server handler exists for op3, op6 or UseItemVital, and nothing here is runtime-captured. Report-only additive; ledger stays 25. Verified by tools/pf_use_drop_sell_static.py (88 guards, exit 0) and tests/test_use_drop_sell_static.py (16 tests).

capabilities.title: Client-requested logout is acknowledged and closes the session cleanly
capabilities.notes: HYP-PF-012 (owner option A, 2026-08-17): both captured LogoutVital forms (subcode 01 exit-game, 03 return-to-character-select) are acknowledged with a designed hash-pinned echo behind the logout opt-in scenario only, after sessions.closed_at commits; the dispatch layer is silent afterward and everything else fails closed. The wire/DB layer is loopback-tested and headless-proven (LOGOUT-ACK-001), and GT-007 (2026-08-17 attended, reports/PF_GT007_LOGOUT_ECHO_ACK_CLIENT_TRANSITION_NEGATIVE_20260817.md) confirmed close-before-ack on the real client for the first time. GT-007 also falsified the echo-only shape at the client-observable layer: the real client neither returns to character select (03) nor closes itself (01) on the echo ack, though the no-response freeze from GT-002 did not recur. The row stays in_progress until a content-bearing response shape (03: character-select/world payload; 01: close instruction or server-side socket close) is designed under a new hypothesis and passes the attended client-observable check. HYP-PF-013 (LOGOUT-CLOSE-001, round 43 under the owner's standing pre-approval) implements the server-side-close branch: unchanged PF-012 ack bytes plus a clean shutdown+close of the accepted GAME socket 250 ms after the ack, behind the separate ack_close opt-in scenario, fail-closed without an attached transport lever. The client-observable check for this shape is queued as GT-008; a disconnect-error dialog would route design to the recorded 0x3D4B-first fallback under a new entry. UPDATE 2026-08-18 (attended GT-008, รอบใหญ่ #2): the ack+close shape (HYP-PF-013, ack then clean server-side socket shutdown at +250 ms) is also falsified at the client-observable layer -- the client never detects the TCP close at all on either subcode (no transition, no dialog, UI live 40+ s). Client transitions are protocol-driven, not transport-driven; next design = 0x3D4B-first response (world/character-select payload before or instead of the bare echo), to open as a new ledger entry when implemented. UPDATE 2026-08-18 (chief round 53): HYP-PF-016 (LOGOUT-RESP-001) implements the 0x3D4B-first design behind the new worldinfo_first opt-in scenario: the full-form 248-byte GetWorldInfoVital payload the client itself sends at logout-dialog open is stored in memory per connection (never written), and an accepted LogoutVital is answered response-first -- the stored payload mirror-echoed in the accepted RuntimeRes v4 collection envelope with the client's own count=3 and the DELETE-SOFT-002 trailing mask (270-byte PC / 283-byte frame), then the unchanged PF-012 ack, then the composed PF-013 close at +250 ms; sessions.closed_at still commits before the first response byte, and a session that never sent the full form stays silent (no ack-only fallback). Headless-proven in the sandbox over real TCP (ordering and bytes pinned, negative silent, latest-payload-wins). Whether the real client finally transitions (03: character select; 01: exit) is queued as GT-013.

capabilities.title: Server-side movement validation and authoritative correction
capabilities.notes: MOVE-AUTHORITY-001 (chief round 72, 2026-08-18) characterizes, byte-exact from the read-only client binary cross-checked against the read-only server source, the transport the local player's movement report rides and confirms the acceptance-as-given gap. The report (the frame the client emits when it walks or clicks a destination) rides TargetPosVital 0x2A90. Identity follows the runtime-assigned id wall of the ItemOperateVitalReq/ECHO/TELEPORT cohort: the RTTI name string 'TargetPosVital' sits at 0xF30818, a single registration site 0xBEE380 stores the runtime id into id-slot 0x1081FE0, the id 0x2A90 is never a code immediate anywhere in .text (dword scan, rel32 tails excluded, zero hits), and the id-slot is read by exactly one get-id stub 0x5E50A0. The vtable 0xF30230 carries the shared VitalData const 0x401B20 at +0x08, get-id at +0x10, and the serializer 0x5E50E0 at +0x18; the constructor 0x5E5050 zero-inits four f32 (x,y,z,heading at obj+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20) and two u8 (moving,mask at obj+0x24/+0x25). The wire schema is four f32 (tag 0x2A) then two u8 (tag 0x0B): serializer 0x5E50E0 emits x,y,z through the vec3 helper 0x5F3490 and heading through the field serializer 0x89A600 (stdcall (tag,ptr,width) ret 0xC), then moving and mask; this matches the server parse_target_pos_vital byte-for-byte. The authentic captured payload V139_MARKER1_TARGETPOS_PC embedded in the server source decodes under this schema to MARKER1 (x,y,z)=(-10322,-755,671), heading 0, moving 1, mask 0, remain 0. Producer: the object is factory-constructed (0x28-byte allocation) then the ctor is called from exactly two sites (0x44B7C4, 0x44B842); get-id and the serializer are vtable-dispatched (no direct E8 callers), consistent with the cohort. Server coverage gap: the server decodes the identical schema and stores self.last_target_pos = (x, y, z, heading), performing no local-player speed/distance/collision/line-of-sight validation and sending no corrective reposition; the only movement_speed in the file is the NPC walk-speed constant V73_WALK_SPEED fed to NPCAttr. Still not claimed: the original server's authority model itself (accept threshold, correction packet, cadence) is uncaptured, so this is characterization only. Stays in_progress, not runtime_pass: no authority behavior is implemented and no validation event is captured; the next hop is a corpus of additional movement frames or a live capture of an authoritative correction (queued alongside GT-011..GT-015). MOVE-AUTHORITY-002 (chief round 116, cloud, HYP-PF-030) closes the CODE half of that gap behind an opt-in scenario and leaves the grade where it is: the server now decides, per reported TargetPosVital singleton, whether the durable position write may happen at all, measured against the authoritative character row, and WITHHOLDS it when the reading exceeds our own step, vertical or speed budget. The lane composes no bytes for the frame in hand -- gated and ungated sessions return the same action list -- because no captured frame, producer or consumer for a server-initiated corrective reposition exists, so none is invented; the withheld write does change the position bytes of the NEXT login's StartGame, which is proven headless rather than assumed. Proven at the wire/DB layer only (63 tests, an 87-guard offline verifier the suite executes, a refused reading never becoming the next baseline, and an admitted reading recorded only after the durable write survived). Two shipped budgets were falsified by committed evidence before the checkpoint landed, by replaying MOVE-CADENCE-001's authentic 29-reading walk through the ladder: enforcing the client's moving flag would have refused 23 of 29 readings, and dividing by a below-floor elapsed refused an ordinary reading because two readings shared one heartbeat. Known gaps are recorded in the report rather than hidden, the largest being that exactly one reading per server-initiated teleport is admitted without being measured. The budgets remain OUR design and are validated against that one walk and nothing else; no client has ever been run against this lane, which is the queued attended test, and this row does not move until it has run.

capabilities.title: NPC walk and run gait presentation

Observed visually for a fixed set of placements in the legacy scenario runner; it is not a general locomotion or pathing engine. The Foundation population path never requests a movement speed, so no Foundation runtime has reproduced this gait and a test pins that absence.

capabilities.title: Another player's movement projected to a second client
capabilities.notes: MOVE-PROJECT-001 (chief round 73, 2026-08-18) characterizes, byte-exact from the read-only client binary cross-checked against the read-only server source, the mechanism by which a remote actor's position/heading/control state is projected on the client. That state rides the MovementAttr (MOVEMENT_ATTR = 0x2067) attribute carried inside every remote-actor entry of the RuntimeRes actor stream. Identity follows the runtime-assigned id wall of the TargetPosVital/ItemOperate cohort: the class name string 'MovementAttr' sits at 0xF0E840, a single registration site 0xBD9410 stores the runtime id into id-slot 0x10334A8, the id 0x2067 is never a code immediate anywhere in .text (dword scan, rel32 tails excluded, zero hits), and the id-slot is written by exactly one site 0xBD9421 and read by exactly one get-id stub 0x43BBB0. The MovementAttr class token 0x103346C is the is-a reference used by the runtime type check 0x88F2B0 at all three consumers that downcast an incoming attr (0x465466, the delta 0x46705A, the apply/merge 0x467145). The vtable 0xF0D0F8 carries the shared framework const 0x401B20 at +0x08, get-id 0x43BBB0 at +0x10, reset 0x467030 at +0x28, delta 0x467040 at +0x2C, apply/merge 0x467130 at +0x30, and Serial 0x4671C0 at +0x34; the payload layout is identity qword at obj+0x18, submask u8 at +0x20, position vec3 at +0x28..+0x30, heading f32 at +0x34, mode u8 at +0x38, flags u32 at +0x3C, three f32 at +0x40/+0x44/+0x48, and the field mask u8 at +0x4C. The wire schema (Serial 0x4671C0; the codec 0x89A600 is stdcall (tag,ptr,width) ret 0xC and direction-agnostic, so the same routine decodes an inbound attr): header 0x467790 emits u8(tag 0x0B,1) submask then a qword(tag 0x32) identity, then the field mask u8(tag 0x0B), then per set bit position vec3 via helper 0x5F3490 (three tag-0x2A f32), heading f32(tag 0x2A), mode u8(tag 0x0B), flags u32(tag 0x26), and three f32(tag 0x2A) -- byte-exact with the server make_remote_movement_attr. The projection apply/merge 0x467130 is the consumer: after the 0x88F2B0/0x103346C is-a guard it reads the target's own field mask at +0x4C and, for every field whose bit is NOT set, copies that field from the incoming source into the same offset (position +0x28/+0x30, heading +0x34, mode +0x38, flags +0x3C, f32 +0x40/+0x44/+0x48), so a sparse movement delta is completed against the existing projected state without overwriting fields the target already owns. The delta mask 0x467040 is the outbound counterpart, clearing the mask then setting each bit whose field differs from a reference (position via 0x4A1720, heading and the three f32 via cvtps2pd+ucomisd, mode via u8 cmp, flags via u32 cmp). Server cross-check: MOVEMENT_ATTR = 0x2067; make_remote_movement_attr documents the same static 0x4671C0 per-field mask and emits the byte-exact schema; make_remote_actor_entry (client serializer 0x5E21D0) carries it as u16tag(0x12, 0x2067) followed by the attr's Serial. Still not claimed: the server only ever emits remote actors of actor_type 4 (CNetNPC); no authentic capture of a remote human-PLAYER actor_type and its full projected-attr composition exists, so this characterizes the projection mechanism byte-exact but does not claim the original server's remote human-player projection behavior. Report-only additive: no server behavior changed; ledger stays 25. capabilities.title: Channels, whisper and broadcast routing
capabilities.notes: CHAT-CHANNEL-001 (chief round 75, 2026-08-18) retires the 'Channel identifiers and recipient resolution are uncaptured' half of this row's gap with byte-exact static evidence from the read-only client binary, cross-checked against the read-only server source. The client carries a family of seventeen Channel_*Vital classes registered from one contiguous block 0xBF72B0..0xBF74F0 (stride 0x20, eighteen entries = the seventeen channels plus CBoardcastVital) in exactly the PF-NAMEID-HASH-001 shape, so the previously proven name hash (client 0x89B220, u16 id = sum over i of (int16)((signed char)name[i]*(i+1)) mod 2^16) derives every channel id from the in-image name literal alone. The anchor holds exactly: name_id('Channel_LocalTalkMessageVital') = 0xAC52, the id GT-006 captured on the wire. The full table is ForbidTalkNotification 0xFDF2, LocalTalkMessage 0xAC52, LocalPerformance 0xAE8C, PartyMessage 0x82E6, Whisper 0x556C, GuildMessage 0x8189, ActorBoardcastMessage 0xEDFA, GMGlobalMessage 0x9F2C, JoinCustomChannel 0xBA58, OnActorJoinCustomChannel 0x18DA, LeaveCustomChannel 0xC663, OnActorLeaveCustomChannel 0x2770, CustomChannelMessage 0xE064, JoinOriginalSinChannel 0xFA07, OriginalSinChannelMessage 0x265C, JoinClassChannel 0xAC9D, ClassChannelMessage 0xD1F8 -- no collisions. All seventeen ids obey the runtime-assigned wall (zero code immediates once rel32 tails of E8/E9 AND 0F 8x are excluded -- the jcc exclusion matters, without it LocalPerformance's 0xAE8C takes two false positives from 0F 8C AE 00 00 00), each id-slot has exactly one writer and one reader, and two independent naming routes converge 17/17 (literal -> thunk -> slot -> get-id -> vtable+0x10, and vtable+0x00 -> type node -> registration -> .?AVChannel_XxxVital@@ descriptor). Serialize is vtable +0x18, one bidirectional thiscall (bool save, Stream*) ret 8 routine whose bl selects the write or read codec, so the same routine decodes inbound; the wstring codec 0x89A810/0x89A880 is tag 0x48 + u32 byte-length + UTF-16LE, and the scalar codec is the same 0x89A600 stdcall (tag,ptr,width) ret 0xC used by MOVE-PROJECT-001. Recipient resolution is decoded: Channel_WhisperVital is the only channel with a third wstring, its Serialize 0x65AEA0 emitting speaker@+0x34, body@+0x18, recipient@+0x50 and a u8 (tag 0x0B) @+0x6C, with Whisper's own ctor 0x658240 constructing +0x50 and zeroing +0x6C so the field belongs to Whisper rather than the base; the dispatcher reads that u8 as a result code (1 -> system message 0x0B, 2 -> 0x18, otherwise render as WhisperTalk). Five channels share the base Channel_MessageVtial serializer 0x65AD40 (LocalTalk, Party, Guild, ActorBoardcast, GMGlobal), so their wire is byte-identical and the channel identifier IS the 16-bit class id rather than any selector inside the payload. The 34-byte GT-006 replay payload parses through that schema with zero bytes left over (48 00000000 empty-wstring speaker, then 48 18000000 and 24 bytes of UTF-16LE 'PFCHATPROBE1'), upgrading CHAT-ECHO-002's opaque prefix into named fields. The routing hierarchy is readable from the type-node registration block 0xBF74F0..0xBF7AB0 (23 entries carrying a parent node argument): Channel_BasicVtial -> {Channel_CommandVtial (7 leaves), Channel_MessageVtial, Channel_ForbidTalkNotificationVtial}, and Channel_MessageVtial -> {Channel_GlobalVital (7 leaves), Channel_LocalVital (2 leaves: LocalTalk and Party)}; the five base classes have no literal and no thunk, so they have no wire id. Join and Leave are a real membership protocol: every Join*/Leave* schema ends in a u8 result and its delivery hook is gated on that byte, suppressing hand-off into ChannelModule_Client when it is non-zero (0x65C8B0 gates +0x3D, 0x65C950 gates +0x21, 0x65CB40 gates +0x24, each offset matching that channel's trailing u8 exactly), while the OnActor* counterparts share serializer 0x65B140 and add the actor-name wstring. Client-side routing resolves through vtable +0x1C into the module registry [0x1032EC4]+0x130 by the ASCII name 'ChannelModule_Client', reaching dispatcher 0x659870, an ordered downcast chain over fourteen channels with per-channel style names (LocalTalk, WhisperTalk, GuildTalk, PartyTalk, YellTalk, LocalPerformance, CustomDefine, ClassTalk). Evidenced negative: JoinOriginalSinChannel, OriginalSinChannelMessage and JoinClassChannel have no downcast consumer anywhere in .text, so three of the seventeen are producer-side only. Server gap, now measured: v141 contains no Channel_ token and none of the seventeen ids, and only src/pirateforce_foundation/chat_input_hypothesis.py touches one of them (0xAC52), still calling it UNKNOWN_0xAC52 and comparing it as one opaque pinned blob -- seventeen channels client-side, one touched server-side, zero decoded server-side. Not claimed: the original server's fan-out, routing or membership authority behaviour, which still needs two concurrent sessions and has never been established by any runtime pass, so this stays in_progress and not runtime_pass; also unclaimed are the value semantics of each result code and of the u8 tag 0x08, u8@+0x3C and u16@+0x28 fields. Report-only additive; ledger stays 25. Verified by tools/pf_chat_channel_family_static.py (69 guards, exit 0) and tests/test_chat_channel_family_static.py (15 tests). CHAT-CHANNEL-002 (chief round 76, 2026-08-18, HYP-PF-019) converts that static reading into a working server-side codec and takes the first real bite out of the routing half. The shared serializer 0x65AD40 is now implemented both directions -- decode payload -> (speaker, body) and encode (channel, speaker, body) -> payload -- against the wstring codec tag 0x48 + u32 byte-length + UTF-16LE, and the decode is not self-certified: re-encoding the decoded GT-006 probes reproduces both 34-byte captured payloads byte-for-byte, and composing them into the accepted RuntimeRes v4 envelope reproduces the PC and frame sha256 that the independent CHAT-ECHO-002 lane pinned by a code path that never parsed anything. A pin that can only be hit by getting field order, tag, length width and endianness all correct simultaneously is the strongest available substitute for a capture. The five shared-serializer channels are shown to differ in exactly two bytes of the composed PC (pc[16:18] = the 16-bit class id), which is the CHAT-CHANNEL-001 channel-id-is-the-selector conclusion re-proven on bytes the server itself produced. The lane is opt-in only (scenarios/channel_message_hypothesis_shared_serializer.json, test_only, production_allowed false, database_write none), is not imported by runtime.py, app.py, connection.py or scenario.py, and fails closed on non-member channel ids (Whisper 0x556C is rejected on purpose -- its schema carries a third wstring and a result byte), short headers, tag mismatch, odd byte lengths, lengths past the payload end, trailing bytes, surrogate or non-BMP text, and empty bodies. STILL NOT CLAIMED, and this is the load-bearing limit: only 0xAC52 has ever been seen on this project's wire in either direction. The other four channels' pins say 'if the server sends this, these are the bytes', not 'this was captured'; whether the original protocol even permitted the server to originate them is unproven, as is what the client renders for any of them -- that is GT-016, which this milestone unblocks. CHAT-CHANNEL-003 (chief round 77, 2026-08-18, same HYP-PF-019) closes the one gap CHAT-CHANNEL-002 left on purpose: the codec had no way to reach the wire, so GT-016 was unblocked in principle and BLOCKED in practice. A second opt-in file scenarios/channel_message_hypothesis_channel_sweep.json plus the new CLI flag --channel-message-hypothesis-scenario (explicit --db required, mutually exclusive with every other scenario mode including --chat-input-hypothesis-scenario, which keys on the same vital id) wires the lane into runtime.py: one accepted 34-byte ascii12 0xAC52 frame, under the unchanged selected + runtime-ready guards, is decoded via decode_channel_message_payload -- decoded, not spliced -- and answered with five composed frames, one per shared-serializer channel, in the declared order LocalTalk, Party, Guild, GMGlobal, ActorBoardcast, labelled HYP_PF_019_CHANNEL_SWEEP_<CHANNEL> and spaced 3.0 s apart so an attended reader can tell five lines from one burst. Proven headless through the real make_state_class dispatch path (tests/test_channel_message_dispatch.py, 25 tests): five actions in pinned order; the five nested payloads identical byte for byte at 34 bytes and one sha256, because the speaker is empty on all five by policy; the five composed PCs differing in exactly two bytes, pc[16:18], measured on dispatched bytes rather than fixture bytes; all ten per-channel PC/frame hashes matching the scenario pins; two requests giving ten frames with no accumulated state; the temp database file byte-identical across a whole sweep window and across refused frames; every fail-closed path (wrong length, wrong prefix, wrong text bytes, wrong envelope, no selected character, not-yet-runtime-ready) returning zero actions with a named no-reply event; and with no scenario the GT-006 baseline byte-identical. The containment test that asserted 'no runtime module imports this lane' was deliberately rewritten rather than worked around -- the importer list is now exact (app.py, runtime.py), connection.py and scenario.py still never mention it, every runtime mention is inside the scenario gate, and both profiles keep test_only true / production_allowed false / database_write none. STILL NOT CLAIMED and unchanged by this milestone: no client has ever seen a sweep, so whether any of the five renders, with what channel tag, and whether 3.0 s separates them on screen is exactly GT-016; unlike CHAT-ECHO-002 this lane has not been driven through a real server process over TCP, only through the dispatcher; and nothing here is fan-out, routing or membership -- a sweep is five frames back to the one connection that asked. Ledger stays 26 (HYP-PF-019 amended, tracked_versions CHAT-CHANNEL-002 -> +CHAT-CHANNEL-003). Row stays in_progress and not runtime_pass.
